classification_basis: Implemented entries were reviewed against the official page, fixtures, and both engines. Summaries, analysis classes, and delegation recommendations for unimplemented entries were drafted from the official page and assigned a status by the documented rules in docs/architecture/sei-cert-rule-pack.md; review them against the official page before promoting an entry.

rules.title: Do not form or use out-of-bounds pointers or array subscripts
rules.summary: Every pointer computed or dereferenced and every array index used must stay within the bounds of its array object, or at most one past the end for pointers not dereferenced.
rules.noncompliant_concept: Indexing or pointer arithmetic with an unchecked or off-by-one value reaching outside the array.
rules.compliant_concept: Validates indices and offsets against the actual element count before forming or using them.
false_positive_risks: If implemented as a syntax-only rule: Flags every variable subscript even when a dominating bounds check or loop invariant already guarantees validity.
false_negative_risks: This rule pack contains no detection for this rule; an absence of findings is not evidence of compliance.
Syntax-only detection limit: Cannot know array sizes or index ranges across calls, aliasing, or heap allocations; misses tainted offsets.

rules.title: Ensure size arguments for variable length arrays are in a valid range
rules.summary: The size expression of a variable length array must be validated to be positive and small enough to avoid stack exhaustion or size overflow before the array is declared.
rules.noncompliant_concept: Declaring a VLA whose length derives from an unchecked or attacker-influenced value.
rules.compliant_concept: Range-checks the length against zero and a sane maximum, or uses bounded heap allocation instead.
false_positive_risks: If implemented as a syntax-only rule: Flags all VLAs including those with already-validated sizes; checking for nearby guards syntactically is unreliable.
false_negative_risks: This rule pack contains no detection for this rule; an absence of findings is not evidence of compliance.
Syntax-only detection limit: Cannot judge whether a guard is sufficient or whether sizeof of the VLA type overflows.

rules.title: Do not subtract or compare two pointers that do not refer to the same array
rules.summary: Pointer subtraction and relational comparison are only defined between pointers into the same array object (or one past it).
rules.noncompliant_concept: Subtracting or ordering pointers that refer to different, unrelated objects.
rules.compliant_concept: Compares or subtracts only pointers derived from a single array, using indices otherwise.

exceptions.summary: Relational comparison of pointers into different members of one struct object is allowed.

false_positive_risks: If implemented as a syntax-only rule: Most pointer subtractions are legitimate; syntax alone cannot tell whether both operands share a base object.
false_negative_risks: This rule pack contains no detection for this rule; an absence of findings is not evidence of compliance.
Syntax-only detection limit: Pointers originating from different objects via parameters or globals look identical to valid ones.

rules.title: Do not add or subtract an integer to a pointer to a non-array object
rules.summary: Integer addition or subtraction on a pointer is only permitted when the pointer refers to an element of an array, not to a scalar or individual struct member.
rules.noncompliant_concept: Treating a pointer to a lone variable or struct member as an array and offsetting it.
rules.compliant_concept: Uses real arrays or named struct members instead of offsetting from a non-array object.

exceptions.summary: A lone non-array object may be treated as a one-element array for pointer arithmetic.

false_positive_risks: If implemented as a syntax-only rule: Pointer parameters usually do point into arrays; flagging all arithmetic on them is very noisy.
false_negative_risks: This rule pack contains no detection for this rule; an absence of findings is not evidence of compliance.
Syntax-only detection limit: Needs to know what object the pointer was derived from, often across function boundaries.

rules.title: Guarantee that library functions do not form invalid pointers
rules.summary: Pointer and size arguments passed to library functions such as memcpy, memset, or fread must describe a region entirely within valid objects.
rules.noncompliant_concept: Calling a memory or I/O library function with a length larger than the source or destination object.
rules.compliant_concept: Derives the length from the actual object size and checks it against both buffers.
false_positive_risks: If implemented as a syntax-only rule: Every memcpy with a non-constant length would match; syntax cannot compare length with buffer size.
false_negative_risks: This rule pack contains no detection for this rule; an absence of findings is not evidence of compliance.
Syntax-only detection limit: Requires object size and value-range reasoning; wrong element-versus-byte counts look normal syntactically.

rules.title: Do not add or subtract a scaled integer to a pointer
rules.summary: Integers added to or subtracted from typed pointers must not already be multiplied by sizeof, since pointer arithmetic scales automatically.
rules.noncompliant_concept: Adding an offset scaled by sizeof or offsetof to a non-byte pointer.
rules.compliant_concept: Adds an unscaled element count, or performs byte arithmetic through an unsigned char pointer.
false_positive_risks: If implemented as a syntax-only rule: Byte pointers (char, unsigned char) legitimately use sizeof offsets; requires pointee type to distinguish.
false_negative_risks: This rule pack contains no detection for this rule; an absence of findings is not evidence of compliance.
Syntax-only detection limit: Misses scaled values computed earlier and stored in a variable before being added.

rules.title: Clean up thread-specific storage
rules.summary: Memory associated with thread-specific storage keys must be released, via a destructor or explicit freeing, before the thread or key goes away.
rules.noncompliant_concept: Allocating storage via tss_set without a destructor or explicit free, leaking it per thread.
rules.compliant_concept: Registers a cleanup destructor with tss_create or frees the value before thread exit and tss_delete.
false_positive_risks: If implemented as a syntax-only rule: tss_create with NULL destructor may be fine when values are freed manually elsewhere.
false_negative_risks: This rule pack contains no detection for this rule; an absence of findings is not evidence of compliance.
Syntax-only detection limit: Leak depends on thread lifetime and paths where cleanup is skipped; not visible syntactically.

rules.title: Do not destroy a mutex while it is locked
rules.summary: A mutex must not be destroyed while it is locked or while other threads may still be waiting on it.
rules.noncompliant_concept: Calling mtx_destroy while some thread still holds or blocks on the mutex.
rules.compliant_concept: Destroys the mutex only after all threads using it have been joined or have released it.
false_positive_risks: Paths on which the lock call failed but the code continues to destroy are reported.
false_negative_risks: Mutexes locked by another thread, destroyed in another function, or reached through aliases require concurrency analysis.
Engines do not preprocess: code produced by macro expansion, conditional compilation, or code generation is not analyzed.

implementation.coverage_note: Same-function lock followed by destroy without an intervening unlock (POSIX and C11).

rules.title: Prevent data races when accessing bit-fields from multiple threads
rules.summary: Adjacent bit-fields share a storage unit, so concurrent writes to different bit-fields of one object need common synchronization.
rules.noncompliant_concept: Different threads updating neighboring bit-fields of the same struct without a shared lock.
rules.compliant_concept: Protects all bit-fields in a storage unit with one mutex, or uses separate non-bit-field members.
false_positive_risks: If implemented as a syntax-only rule: Bit-field writes in single-threaded or already-locked contexts would be reported.
false_negative_risks: This rule pack contains no detection for this rule; an absence of findings is not evidence of compliance.
Syntax-only detection limit: Requires knowing which objects are shared between threads and what locks guard them.

rules.title: Avoid race conditions when using library functions
rules.summary: Library functions that keep internal static state or return shared buffers must not be called concurrently from multiple threads without protection.
rules.noncompliant_concept: Calling non-reentrant functions like strtok, strerror, or localtime from several threads.
rules.compliant_concept: Uses reentrant variants (e.g., strtok_r, strerror_r) or serializes calls with a lock.
false_positive_risks: If implemented as a syntax-only rule: Flags these calls in programs that are single-threaded or already serialize them.
false_negative_risks: This rule pack contains no detection for this rule; an absence of findings is not evidence of compliance.
Syntax-only detection limit: Unlisted or platform-specific non-reentrant functions and wrapper functions escape name matching.

rules.title: Declare objects shared between threads with appropriate storage durations
rules.summary: Objects whose addresses are shared with other threads must have a storage duration that outlives every thread that uses them.
rules.noncompliant_concept: Passing the address of a local or thread-local variable to a thread that may outlive it.
rules.compliant_concept: Shares static, allocated, or otherwise long-lived objects, or joins before the local goes out of scope.
false_positive_risks: If implemented as a syntax-only rule: Passing a local address to thrd_create is safe when the creator joins before returning.
false_negative_risks: This rule pack contains no detection for this rule; an absence of findings is not evidence of compliance.
Syntax-only detection limit: Escape through structures, globals, or helper calls hides the stack address handoff.

rules.title: Avoid deadlock by locking in a predefined order
rules.summary: When multiple mutexes are acquired, every thread must lock them in one consistent global order to prevent circular wait and deadlock.
rules.noncompliant_concept: Two code paths acquiring the same pair of locks in opposite orders.
rules.compliant_concept: Defines a canonical ordering (e.g., by address or id) and always locks in that order.
false_positive_risks: If implemented as a syntax-only rule: Nested lock calls are not deadlocks if ordering is consistent elsewhere; syntax sees only one function.
false_negative_risks: This rule pack contains no detection for this rule; an absence of findings is not evidence of compliance.
Syntax-only detection limit: Lock order inversions span functions and depend on which runtime objects alias.

rules.title: Wrap functions that can spuriously wake up in a loop
rules.summary: Waits on condition variables can return without a signal, so each wait must sit inside a loop that rechecks the condition predicate.
rules.noncompliant_concept: Calling cnd_wait or cnd_timedwait guarded by an if or not guarded at all.
rules.compliant_concept: Calls the wait inside a while loop that tests the condition predicate.
false_positive_risks: A wait guarded by a loop in a caller is reported.
false_negative_risks: A loop that does not re-test the predicate is accepted as compliant.
Engines do not preprocess: code produced by macro expansion, conditional compilation, or code generation is not analyzed.

implementation.coverage_note: Condition-variable waits not lexically inside a loop.

rules.title: Do not call signal() in a multithreaded program
rules.summary: signal() must not be used in a program that runs multiple threads, since its behavior is undefined there.
rules.noncompliant_concept: Installing a handler with signal() in code that also creates threads.
rules.compliant_concept: Uses sigaction or a dedicated signal-handling mechanism suited to threaded programs.

exceptions.summary: Platforms like POSIX that define signal-handler behavior in multithreaded programs are exempt.

false_positive_risks: If implemented as a syntax-only rule: signal() in programs that never create threads would be flagged without whole-program context.
false_negative_risks: This rule pack contains no detection for this rule; an absence of findings is not evidence of compliance.
Syntax-only detection limit: Thread creation in another translation unit or library makes the program multithreaded invisibly.

rules.title: Preserve thread safety and liveness when using condition variables
rules.summary: Condition variable signaling must preserve safety and liveness: a single-thread wakeup is only valid when any waiting thread can make progress.
rules.noncompliant_concept: Using cnd_signal when waiters have different predicates, so the wrong thread may wake and stall.
rules.compliant_concept: Uses cnd_broadcast, or distinct condition variables per predicate so cnd_signal wakes a suitable waiter.
false_positive_risks: If implemented as a syntax-only rule: Most cnd_signal uses are correct; flagging them all is noisy.
false_negative_risks: This rule pack contains no detection for this rule; an absence of findings is not evidence of compliance.
Syntax-only detection limit: Determining heterogeneous waiter predicates requires multi-thread semantic reasoning.

rules.title: Do not join or detach a thread that was previously joined or detached
rules.summary: A thread must be joined or detached at most once; a second join or detach on the same thread is undefined.
rules.noncompliant_concept: Calling thrd_join or thrd_detach on a thread already joined or detached.
rules.compliant_concept: Tracks each thread handle so exactly one join or detach occurs.
false_positive_risks: If implemented as a syntax-only rule: Same handle variable may be reassigned between calls, making repeated calls legitimate.
false_negative_risks: This rule pack contains no detection for this rule; an absence of findings is not evidence of compliance.
Syntax-only detection limit: Join and detach often occur in different functions or threads.

rules.title: Do not refer to an atomic variable twice in an expression
rules.summary: An atomic object should be referenced only once per expression, because separate atomic accesses within one expression do not form a single atomic operation.
rules.noncompliant_concept: An expression reading and writing the same atomic variable through separate accesses, e.g., a = a * 2.
rules.compliant_concept: Uses one atomic read-modify-write function or compare-exchange loop for the combined update.
false_positive_risks: If implemented as a syntax-only rule: Needs type information to know the variable is atomic; may flag non-atomic lookalikes.
false_negative_risks: This rule pack contains no detection for this rule; an absence of findings is not evidence of compliance.
Syntax-only detection limit: Macros or typedefs hiding _Atomic types, and references through aliases, escape matching.

rules.title: Wrap functions that can fail spuriously in a loop
rules.summary: Operations allowed to fail spuriously, like weak compare-exchange, must be retried in a loop until they succeed or a real mismatch occurs.
rules.noncompliant_concept: Calling atomic_compare_exchange_weak once without a retry loop.
rules.compliant_concept: Places the weak compare-exchange inside a loop, or uses the strong variant.
false_positive_risks: If implemented as a syntax-only rule: Callers that deliberately handle failure by retrying elsewhere would be flagged.
false_negative_risks: This rule pack contains no detection for this rule; an absence of findings is not evidence of compliance.
Syntax-only detection limit: Explicit-memory-order variants or wrappers may be missed by name-based patterns.

rules.title: Do not allow data races in multithreaded code
rules.summary: Shared data accessed by multiple threads, with at least one writer, must be synchronized so no conflicting accesses are unordered.
rules.noncompliant_concept: Threads reading and writing the same non-atomic variable without locks or atomics.
rules.compliant_concept: Guards shared accesses with mutexes or uses atomic types and fences.
false_positive_risks: If implemented as a syntax-only rule: Accesses to globals in single-threaded phases or already-locked regions would be reported.
false_negative_risks: This rule pack contains no detection for this rule; an absence of findings is not evidence of compliance.
Syntax-only detection limit: Identifying shared objects and happens-before relationships is beyond syntax.

rules.title: Declare objects with appropriate storage durations
rules.summary: An object must not be referenced after its lifetime ends; addresses of automatic objects must not escape to longer-lived storage or be returned.
rules.noncompliant_concept: Returning or storing the address of a local variable in a global or output parameter.
rules.compliant_concept: Uses static or allocated storage, or copies values, when data must outlive the function.
false_positive_risks: If implemented as a syntax-only rule: Storing a local address in a struct that does not outlive the frame looks similar to an escape.
false_negative_risks: This rule pack contains no detection for this rule; an absence of findings is not evidence of compliance.
Syntax-only detection limit: Escapes through intermediate pointers, callee storage, or aliasing are invisible to syntax.

rules.title: Declare identifiers before using them
rules.summary: Every identifier, including functions and their return types, must be explicitly declared before use; no implicit int or implicit function declarations.
rules.noncompliant_concept: Calling an undeclared function or omitting a type specifier on a declaration.
rules.compliant_concept: Includes the right headers or prototypes and states every type explicitly.
false_positive_risks: If implemented as a syntax-only rule: Without preprocessing, a declaration provided through an included header appears missing.
false_negative_risks: This rule pack contains no detection for this rule; an absence of findings is not evidence of compliance.
Syntax-only detection limit: Macro-expanded calls and conditional compilation hide implicit declarations from text matching.

rules.title: Do not declare an identifier with conflicting linkage classifications
rules.summary: An identifier must not be declared with both internal and external linkage in the same translation unit.
rules.noncompliant_concept: Declaring a name static in one place and extern or without storage class in another conflicting way.
rules.compliant_concept: Uses consistent linkage specifiers for every declaration of the identifier.
false_positive_risks: If implemented as a syntax-only rule: Shadowed block-scope declarations that are distinct entities may look conflicting.
false_negative_risks: This rule pack contains no detection for this rule; an absence of findings is not evidence of compliance.
Syntax-only detection limit: Declarations spread across headers and macros require full preprocessing and linkage resolution.

rules.title: Do not declare or define a reserved identifier
rules.summary: Programs must not declare or define identifiers reserved for the implementation, such as leading-underscore names, standard library names, or reserved macro names.
rules.noncompliant_concept: Using names like _Foo, __bar, or redefining errno or standard library function names.
rules.compliant_concept: Chooses identifiers outside reserved namespaces, e.g., include guards without leading underscores.

exceptions.summary: A library function may be declared without its header if the declaration matches the standard one.
Defining a macro named like a reserved identifier is fine when its effect is idempotent, for portability.
Compiler and standard-library implementers may use identifiers reserved for the implementation.

false_positive_risks: If implemented as a syntax-only rule: Flags compiler or standard-library implementation code that is permitted to use reserved names.
false_negative_risks: This rule pack contains no detection for this rule; an absence of findings is not evidence of compliance.
Syntax-only detection limit: Reserved future library names and external-linkage collisions need a complete reserved-name list.

rules.title: Use the correct syntax when declaring a flexible array member
rules.summary: A flexible array member must be declared with empty brackets as the final member, not with a size of zero or one.
rules.noncompliant_concept: Ending a struct with a one-element or zero-length array used as a variable-size tail.
rules.compliant_concept: Declares the trailing member with the standard empty-bracket flexible array syntax.
false_positive_risks: If implemented as a syntax-only rule: Genuine one-element arrays at the end of a struct are not always struct hacks.
false_negative_risks: This rule pack contains no detection for this rule; an absence of findings is not evidence of compliance.
Syntax-only detection limit: Struct hack usage is only evident from how the allocation size is computed elsewhere.

rules.title: Avoid information leakage when passing a structure across a trust boundary
rules.summary: Structures passed across a trust boundary must not leak uninitialized padding bytes or bit-field gaps.
rules.noncompliant_concept: Copying a partially initialized struct with padding to user space, a socket, or a file.
rules.compliant_concept: Serializes members individually, zeroes the whole object first, or packs the structure.
false_positive_risks: If implemented as a syntax-only rule: Most struct copies do not cross trust boundaries; syntax cannot identify the boundary.
false_negative_risks: This rule pack contains no detection for this rule; an absence of findings is not evidence of compliance.
Syntax-only detection limit: Needs layout knowledge of padding and identification of trust-boundary sinks.

rules.title: Do not create incompatible declarations of the same function or object
rules.summary: All declarations of the same function or object across the program must have compatible types.
rules.noncompliant_concept: Declaring an external object or function with a different type in another translation unit.
rules.compliant_concept: Places a single declaration in a shared header included by definer and users.
false_positive_risks: If implemented as a syntax-only rule: Same names in different static scopes or distinct programs may be reported as conflicting.
false_negative_risks: This rule pack contains no detection for this rule; an absence of findings is not evidence of compliance.
Syntax-only detection limit: Incompatibilities only appear when comparing declarations across translation units after preprocessing.

rules.title: Do not declare variables inside a switch statement before the first case label
rules.summary: Variables must not be declared and initialized inside a switch body before the first case label, since the initialization never executes.
rules.noncompliant_concept: Declaring an initialized variable at the top of a switch body above any case label.
rules.compliant_concept: Declares and initializes the variable before the switch statement.
false_positive_risks: If implemented as a syntax-only rule: Few false positives; nested blocks or labels inside macros may confuse a pattern.
false_negative_risks: This rule pack contains no detection for this rule; an absence of findings is not evidence of compliance.
Syntax-only detection limit: Switch bodies produced by macros, or Duff's-device style layouts, may evade simple patterns.

rules.title: Only call functions with the unsequenced or reproducible attributes if they actually have the asserted property
rules.summary: Functions marked with the unsequenced or reproducible attribute must genuinely meet the asserted properties, such as being effectless, idempotent, stateless, or independent.
rules.noncompliant_concept: Attributing a function as reproducible or unsequenced while it mutates or reads changing state.
rules.compliant_concept: Removes the attribute or rewrites the function so it truly satisfies the asserted properties.
false_positive_risks: If implemented as a syntax-only rule: Writes through pointer parameters may be permitted for reproducible functions; syntax cannot judge.
false_negative_risks: This rule pack contains no detection for this rule; an absence of findings is not evidence of compliance.
Syntax-only detection limit: Effects hidden in callees or through function-pointer types carrying the attribute are missed.

rules.title: Do not modify the object referenced by the return value of certain functions
rules.summary: Strings returned by functions like getenv, setlocale, localeconv, and strerror must be treated as read-only and never modified.
rules.noncompliant_concept: Writing through the pointer returned by getenv or similar functions.
rules.compliant_concept: Copies the returned data into owned storage before modifying it.
false_positive_risks: If implemented as a syntax-only rule: Pointer reassignment before writes would be mistaken for modifying the returned object.
false_negative_risks: This rule pack contains no detection for this rule; an absence of findings is not evidence of compliance.
Syntax-only detection limit: Aliases passed to other functions, or casts away of const, hide the modification.

rules.title: Do not rely on an environment pointer following an operation that may invalidate it
rules.summary: An environment pointer such as main's envp must not be relied upon after operations that may modify or reallocate the environment.
rules.noncompliant_concept: Iterating envp after calling setenv or putenv.
rules.compliant_concept: Uses the global environ variable or getenv after environment modifications.
false_positive_risks: If implemented as a syntax-only rule: Using envp only before any modification is fine but pattern-matching ordering is fragile.
false_negative_risks: This rule pack contains no detection for this rule; an absence of findings is not evidence of compliance.
Syntax-only detection limit: Environment changes inside called functions are not visible to local syntax.

rules.title: All exit handlers must return normally
rules.summary: Functions registered as exit handlers must return normally and must not call exit functions or longjmp out.
rules.noncompliant_concept: An atexit handler that calls exit or longjmp, or otherwise does not return.
rules.compliant_concept: Exit handlers perform cleanup and return without invoking termination routines.
false_positive_risks: If implemented as a syntax-only rule: Termination calls on unreachable paths in handlers would be flagged.
false_negative_risks: This rule pack contains no detection for this rule; an absence of findings is not evidence of compliance.
Syntax-only detection limit: Handlers calling helper functions that terminate, or registration via pointers, are missed.

rules.title: Do not call system()
rules.summary: Programs should not invoke a command processor via system() or similar, since command strings can enable injection and environment-dependent execution.
rules.noncompliant_concept: Calling system() or popen() with a command string, especially one built from external data.
rules.compliant_concept: Uses exec-family or CreateProcess APIs with explicit program paths and argument arrays.

exceptions.summary: Calling system() with a null argument to test for a command processor is allowed.

false_positive_risks: A call to system() or popen() with a constant, fully qualified command is still reported because the rule forbids the call itself.
false_negative_risks: Shell invocation through vector exec forms (execv/execvp with a runtime argv containing "-c"), posix_spawn, or wrapper functions is not detected.
Engines do not preprocess: code produced by macro expansion, conditional compilation, or code generation is not analyzed.

implementation.coverage_note: The system(), popen(), _popen(), and literal exec-shell forms are covered in C and C++; command-processor invocation through runtime argument vectors is not.

rules.title: Do not store pointers returned by certain functions
rules.summary: Pointers returned by getenv, localeconv, strerror, asctime and similar must not be kept across later calls that may overwrite or invalidate them.
rules.noncompliant_concept: Saving a getenv result and using it after a subsequent getenv call.
rules.compliant_concept: Copies the returned string immediately, or uses reentrant alternatives.
false_positive_risks: If implemented as a syntax-only rule: Storing the pointer but using it before any further call is harmless.
false_negative_risks: This rule pack contains no detection for this rule; an absence of findings is not evidence of compliance.
Syntax-only detection limit: Invalidating calls in other functions and stored-pointer aliases escape syntax matching.

rules.title: Take care when reading errno
rules.summary: errno must be set to zero before calls that report errors only through errno, and inspected only after the function signals failure.
rules.noncompliant_concept: Checking errno after a call without resetting it first or without an error return.
rules.compliant_concept: Clears errno before the call and examines it only when the return value indicates an error.
false_positive_risks: If implemented as a syntax-only rule: Reset may occur earlier in another statement or helper, appearing absent locally.
false_negative_risks: This rule pack contains no detection for this rule; an absence of findings is not evidence of compliance.
Syntax-only detection limit: Needs per-function knowledge of which library calls set errno and their error indicators.

rules.title: Do not rely on indeterminate values of errno
rules.summary: After a signal handler runs because of an asynchronous signal and signal() fails inside it, errno is indeterminate and must not be relied on.
rules.noncompliant_concept: Reading errno after signal() fails within a signal handler.
rules.compliant_concept: Avoids inspecting errno in that situation and handles signal() failure without it.
false_positive_risks: If implemented as a syntax-only rule: errno use in handlers invoked synchronously via raise or abort is permitted.
false_negative_risks: This rule pack contains no detection for this rule; an absence of findings is not evidence of compliance.
Syntax-only detection limit: Needs identifying which functions run as signal handlers, often registered elsewhere.

rules.title: Detect and handle standard library errors
rules.summary: Return values of standard library functions that indicate errors must be checked and handled appropriately.
rules.noncompliant_concept: Ignoring the result of malloc, fopen, fseek, snprintf, or similar calls.
rules.compliant_concept: Tests each return value against its documented error indicator and handles failure.

exceptions.summary: Return values may be ignored for functions that cannot fail, return no error indication, or are traditionally unchecked.

false_positive_risks: If implemented as a syntax-only rule: Values captured and checked later, or calls whose failure cannot matter (cast to void), look unchecked.
false_negative_risks: This rule pack contains no detection for this rule; an absence of findings is not evidence of compliance.
Syntax-only detection limit: Results that are stored but compared against the wrong error value look checked.

rules.title: Detect errors when converting a string to a number
rules.summary: Converting strings to numbers must use functions that report errors, and must detect invalid input, out-of-range values, and trailing characters.
rules.noncompliant_concept: Using atoi, atof, or sscanf to parse numbers without error detection.
rules.compliant_concept: Uses strtol-family functions and checks errno, end pointer, and range.
false_positive_risks: scanf-family numeric conversions whose inputs are already validated by the caller are still reported.
false_negative_risks: strtol/strtoul/strtod calls whose errno, end pointer, or range checks are missing require data-flow analysis and are not detected.
Non-literal scanf formats are not analyzed.
Engines do not preprocess: code produced by macro expansion, conditional compilation, or code generation is not analyzed.

implementation.coverage_note: Covers the ato* family in C and C++ and literal scanf-family numeric conversions in C.

rules.title: Do not depend on the order of evaluation for side effects
rules.summary: Expressions must not contain unsequenced side effects on the same object, or unsequenced read and write of it, whose result depends on evaluation order.
rules.noncompliant_concept: Expressions like i = i++ + 1, or arguments that both modify the same variable.
rules.compliant_concept: Splits side effects into separate statements so ordering is explicit.
false_positive_risks: If implemented as a syntax-only rule: Side effects separated by sequence points like && or comma may be misread as unsequenced.
false_negative_risks: This rule pack contains no detection for this rule; an absence of findings is not evidence of compliance.
Syntax-only detection limit: Side effects inside called functions or through aliasing pointers are not visible.

rules.title: Do not access a volatile object through a nonvolatile reference
rules.summary: A volatile-qualified object must not be accessed through an lvalue lacking volatile qualification.
rules.noncompliant_concept: Casting away volatile or assigning a volatile object's address to a non-volatile pointer, then using it.
rules.compliant_concept: Keeps the volatile qualifier on every pointer and lvalue used to access the object.
false_positive_risks: If implemented as a syntax-only rule: Casts may look like they drop volatile when typedefs already include it.
false_negative_risks: This rule pack contains no detection for this rule; an absence of findings is not evidence of compliance.
Syntax-only detection limit: Requires type resolution; qualifiers hidden behind typedefs or void pointers are missed.

rules.title: Do not read uninitialized memory
rules.summary: Automatic variables and allocated memory must be initialized before their values are read.
rules.noncompliant_concept: Reading a local or malloc'd buffer on a path where it was never assigned.
rules.compliant_concept: Initializes variables at declaration or on all paths before any read.

exceptions.summary: Reading uninitialized memory via a non-register unsigned char lvalue is permitted, since it cannot trap.

false_positive_risks: If implemented as a syntax-only rule: Variables initialized through out-parameters or on all feasible paths look uninitialized.
false_negative_risks: This rule pack contains no detection for this rule; an absence of findings is not evidence of compliance.
Syntax-only detection limit: Partial struct initialization and heap buffers read in other functions require dataflow.

rules.title: Do not dereference null pointers
rules.summary: Pointers that may be null must not be dereferenced.
rules.noncompliant_concept: Using a pointer from malloc, a lookup, or a parameter without a null check before dereference.
rules.compliant_concept: Checks the pointer for null before every dereference on all paths.

exceptions.summary: Forms like &*p and &p[i] are not dereferences, so they are allowed even when p is null.

false_positive_risks: If implemented as a syntax-only rule: Pointers guaranteed non-null by callers or invariants would be reported if no explicit check exists.
false_negative_risks: This rule pack contains no detection for this rule; an absence of findings is not evidence of compliance.

rules.title: Do not modify objects with temporary lifetime
rules.summary: Objects with temporary lifetime, like arrays inside struct values returned by functions, must not be modified or accessed after the full expression ends.
rules.noncompliant_concept: Writing into an array member of a struct returned by value directly from a call expression.
rules.compliant_concept: Stores the returned struct in a named variable before accessing or modifying its array.
false_positive_risks: If implemented as a syntax-only rule: Accessing non-array members of returned structs is fine but may be matched.
false_negative_risks: This rule pack contains no detection for this rule; an absence of findings is not evidence of compliance.

rules.title: Do not cast pointers into more strictly aligned pointer types
rules.summary: A pointer must not be converted to a pointer type with a stricter alignment requirement unless the address is known to be suitably aligned.
rules.noncompliant_concept: Casting a char pointer to an int or struct pointer and dereferencing it.
rules.compliant_concept: Copies into a properly aligned object, or ensures alignment via alignas or allocator guarantees.

exceptions.summary: On architectures tolerating misaligned access, misaligned pointers are allowed, though slower.
Casting a pointer is allowed when it is known to be suitably aligned for the target type.

false_positive_risks: If implemented as a syntax-only rule: Casts of malloc results or alignas-declared buffers are aligned yet look identical.
false_negative_risks: This rule pack contains no detection for this rule; an absence of findings is not evidence of compliance.
Syntax-only detection limit: Conversions through void pointers or integers hide the alignment change.

rules.title: Call functions with the correct number and type of arguments
rules.summary: Functions must be called with the number and types of arguments matching their definition, with prototypes in scope.
rules.noncompliant_concept: Calling through mismatched declarations or function-pointer types, or passing wrong argument types.
rules.compliant_concept: Declares full prototypes and calls functions with matching argument count and types.
false_positive_risks: If implemented as a syntax-only rule: Implicit conversions that are benign could be reported without type analysis.
false_negative_risks: This rule pack contains no detection for this rule; an absence of findings is not evidence of compliance.
Syntax-only detection limit: Mismatches across translation units or through casts of function pointers are invisible locally.

rules.title: Do not access a variable through a pointer of an incompatible type
rules.summary: An object must only be accessed through an lvalue of a compatible type (or character type), respecting effective type and aliasing rules.
rules.noncompliant_concept: Reading a float through an int pointer cast, violating strict aliasing.
rules.compliant_concept: Uses memcpy, unions, or character types to reinterpret object representations.
false_positive_risks: If implemented as a syntax-only rule: Casts between compatible types or to char pointers are legal yet look similar.
false_negative_risks: This rule pack contains no detection for this rule; an absence of findings is not evidence of compliance.
Syntax-only detection limit: Aliasing via void pointers and across functions needs effective-type tracking.

rules.title: Do not modify constant objects
rules.summary: Objects defined const must not be modified, including through pointers that have cast away the const qualifier.
rules.noncompliant_concept: Casting away const from an object and writing through the resulting pointer.
rules.compliant_concept: Keeps const qualification and modifies only non-const copies.
false_positive_risks: If implemented as a syntax-only rule: Casting away const from data originally non-const is legal yet matched.
false_negative_risks: This rule pack contains no detection for this rule; an absence of findings is not evidence of compliance.

rules.title: Do not compare padding data
rules.summary: Structures must not be compared with memcmp or similar byte-wise functions when their padding contents are indeterminate.
rules.noncompliant_concept: Using memcmp on two struct objects that contain padding bytes.
rules.compliant_concept: Compares structures member by member.

exceptions.summary: Structures with properly aligned or packed members lacking padding bits may be compared bytewise.

false_positive_risks: If implemented as a syntax-only rule: Packed or padding-free structs can be safely compared bytewise yet match.
false_negative_risks: This rule pack contains no detection for this rule; an absence of findings is not evidence of compliance.
Syntax-only detection limit: Needs struct layout knowledge; comparisons through void pointers hide the struct type.

rules.title: Avoid undefined behavior when using restrict-qualified pointers
rules.summary: Objects accessed through restrict-qualified pointers must not be accessed via other, overlapping pointers within the same scope.
rules.noncompliant_concept: Passing overlapping buffers to memcpy or to functions with restrict parameters.
rules.compliant_concept: Ensures restrict-qualified pointers refer to disjoint objects, using memmove for overlap.
false_positive_risks: If implemented as a syntax-only rule: Restrict-parameter calls with disjoint regions cannot be distinguished syntactically.
false_negative_risks: This rule pack contains no detection for this rule; an absence of findings is not evidence of compliance.
Syntax-only detection limit: Overlap depends on runtime pointer values and offsets across calls.

rules.title: Do not rely on side effects in operands to sizeof, \_Alignof, or \_Generic
rules.summary: Operands of sizeof, _Alignof, and _Generic must not rely on side effects, since those operands are not evaluated (except some VLA cases).
rules.noncompliant_concept: Writing sizeof(i++) or a function call expecting it to execute.
rules.compliant_concept: Performs the side effect in a separate statement and applies sizeof to a plain expression.

exceptions.summary: Volatile-object reads may appear as operands of sizeof, _Alignof, or _Generic idiomatically.

false_positive_risks: If implemented as a syntax-only rule: Function calls in sizeof purely to obtain a return type are harmless but flagged.
false_negative_risks: This rule pack contains no detection for this rule; an absence of findings is not evidence of compliance.
Syntax-only detection limit: Side effects hidden behind macros, or VLA operands, need deeper analysis.

rules.title: Do not perform assignments in selection statements
rules.summary: Assignment operators must not appear in controlling expressions of selection or iteration statements, where they likely indicate mistaken equality tests.
rules.noncompliant_concept: if (x = y) or while (a = b) used where a comparison was probably intended.
rules.compliant_concept: Uses equality comparison or performs the assignment in a separate statement.

exceptions.summary: An assignment is allowed in a condition when its result is directly an operand of a comparison.
An assignment is allowed in a condition when it forms a single parenthesized primary expression.
Assignments are allowed inside function-call arguments or array subscripts within conditions.

false_positive_risks: If implemented as a syntax-only rule: Intentional idioms like while ((c = getchar()) != EOF) match unless the exceptions are encoded.
false_negative_risks: This rule pack contains no detection for this rule; an absence of findings is not evidence of compliance.
Syntax-only detection limit: Assignments hidden in macros or nested ternary contexts may be missed.

rules.title: Do not use a bitwise operator with a Boolean-like operand
rules.summary: Bitwise AND, OR, and XOR must not be applied to Boolean-valued operands such as _Bool or comparison results, where logical operators are likely intended.
rules.noncompliant_concept: Writing a < b & c > d, or combining comparison results with |.
rules.compliant_concept: Uses && and || for logic, or parenthesizes deliberately bitwise expressions.
false_positive_risks: If implemented as a syntax-only rule: Deliberate non-short-circuit bitwise combination of booleans would be reported.
false_negative_risks: This rule pack contains no detection for this rule; an absence of findings is not evidence of compliance.
Syntax-only detection limit: Boolean-like operands via _Bool variables or macros need type information.

rules.title: Do not call va_arg with an argument of the incorrect type
rules.summary: The type given to va_arg must match the promoted type of the corresponding argument actually passed.
rules.noncompliant_concept: Calling va_arg with char, short, or float, or a type different from what callers pass.
rules.compliant_concept: Retrieves arguments using their default-promoted types and matching caller conventions.
false_positive_risks: If implemented as a syntax-only rule: Only promotion-incompatible types are syntactically detectable; others need call-site context.
false_negative_risks: This rule pack contains no detection for this rule; an absence of findings is not evidence of compliance.
Syntax-only detection limit: Mismatches between caller argument types and va_arg types span functions.

rules.title: Exclude user input from format strings
rules.summary: Format strings passed to formatted I/O functions must not contain or be derived from untrusted input.
rules.noncompliant_concept: Passing user-controlled data directly as the format argument to printf-family functions.
rules.compliant_concept: Uses a constant format string such as "%s" with the untrusted data as an argument.
false_positive_risks: A non-literal format that is a trusted constant (for example a const char * initialized from a literal or a translation table) is reported.
false_negative_risks: Untrusted data embedded in a format that also has data arguments, vprintf-family calls, and wrappers are not detected.
Engines do not preprocess: code produced by macro expansion, conditional compilation, or code generation is not analyzed.

implementation.coverage_note: Reports the printf-family and syslog shape in which the format is a non-literal expression with no data arguments; taint origin is not established.

rules.title: Do not perform operations on devices that are only appropriate for files
rules.summary: Programs must not perform ordinary-file operations on names that may refer to devices or special files without verifying the file type.
rules.noncompliant_concept: Opening a user-supplied path with fopen and reading/writing without checking it is a regular file.
rules.compliant_concept: Opens with nonblocking flags and verifies the regular-file type via fstat before use.

exceptions.summary: Deliberately opening known device files is allowed; the checks target user-specified files.

false_positive_risks: If implemented as a syntax-only rule: Paths that are fixed and trusted are not at risk yet match file-open patterns.
false_negative_risks: This rule pack contains no detection for this rule; an absence of findings is not evidence of compliance.
Syntax-only detection limit: Requires knowing paths are attacker-influenced and that type checks are performed correctly.

rules.title: Distinguish between characters read from a file and EOF or WEOF
rules.summary: When reading characters, EOF/WEOF must be distinguished from valid characters, e.g., by keeping the result in an int and checking feof and ferror.
rules.noncompliant_concept: Storing the result of getc or fgetc in a char before comparing to EOF.
rules.compliant_concept: Keeps the return in an int (wint_t for wide) and uses feof/ferror when sizes coincide.

exceptions.summary: Status-returning functions like fclose or scanf may be compared to EOF without further checks.

false_positive_risks: If implemented as a syntax-only rule: Stores into char after a proper EOF check are harmless but resemble the pattern.
false_negative_risks: This rule pack contains no detection for this rule; an absence of findings is not evidence of compliance.
Syntax-only detection limit: Platforms where int and char share size need feof/ferror logic not visible syntactically.

rules.title: Do not assume that fgets() or fgetws() returns a nonempty string when successful
rules.summary: Code must not assume a successful fgets or fgetws read produced a nonempty string, e.g., before indexing length minus one.
rules.noncompliant_concept: Using strlen(buf) - 1 as an index after fgets without checking for zero length.
rules.compliant_concept: Checks for an empty string, or uses strchr to locate the newline.
false_positive_risks: If implemented as a syntax-only rule: strlen minus one patterns guarded by an earlier length check would be flagged.
false_negative_risks: This rule pack contains no detection for this rule; an absence of findings is not evidence of compliance.
Syntax-only detection limit: The index may be computed later or in another function from the stored length.

rules.title: Do not copy a FILE object
rules.summary: FILE objects must not be copied by value; only pointers to the original FILE may be used.
rules.noncompliant_concept: Dereferencing a FILE pointer into a local FILE object and using its address.
rules.compliant_concept: Copies the FILE pointer rather than the FILE structure.
false_positive_risks: If implemented as a syntax-only rule: Rare; mostly typedef or macro confusion.
false_negative_risks: This rule pack contains no detection for this rule; an absence of findings is not evidence of compliance.
Syntax-only detection limit: Copies via memcpy or struct assignment through typedefs may be missed.

rules.title: Do not alternately input and output from a stream without an intervening flush or positioning call
rules.summary: On update streams, output and input must be separated by a flush or positioning call as the standard requires.
rules.noncompliant_concept: Writing to a stream and then reading from it immediately without fflush or fseek.
rules.compliant_concept: Inserts fflush, fseek, fsetpos, or rewind between switching directions.
false_positive_risks: If implemented as a syntax-only rule: Streams not opened in update mode cannot violate this but look identical.
false_negative_risks: This rule pack contains no detection for this rule; an absence of findings is not evidence of compliance.
Syntax-only detection limit: Direction switches may span function calls or loops.

rules.title: Reset strings on fgets() or fgetws() failure
rules.summary: When fgets or fgetws fails, the destination buffer must be reset to a known state before further use.
rules.noncompliant_concept: Using the buffer after fgets returned NULL without clearing it.
rules.compliant_concept: Sets the buffer to an empty string on fgets failure.

exceptions.summary: The buffer need not be reset after failure if it goes out of scope or is never used again.

false_positive_risks: If implemented as a syntax-only rule: Code that discards the buffer after failure does not need a reset.
false_negative_risks: This rule pack contains no detection for this rule; an absence of findings is not evidence of compliance.
Syntax-only detection limit: Later use of the buffer may occur in callers.

rules.title: Do not call getc(), putc(), getwc(), or putwc() with a stream argument that has side effects
rules.summary: getc, putc, getwc, and putwc may be macros, so their stream argument must not have side effects.
rules.noncompliant_concept: Passing an expression like fopen(...) or fp++ as the stream to getc.
rules.compliant_concept: Evaluates the stream into a variable first, or uses fgetc/fputc.
false_positive_risks: If implemented as a syntax-only rule: Function calls without side effects as stream arguments would be flagged.
false_negative_risks: This rule pack contains no detection for this rule; an absence of findings is not evidence of compliance.
Syntax-only detection limit: Side effects hidden in called functions are not syntactically obvious.

rules.title: Close files when they are no longer needed
rules.summary: Files and other resources opened by the program must be closed when no longer needed, before their handle is lost.
rules.noncompliant_concept: Returning or exiting a function while an opened FILE pointer goes out of scope unclosed.
rules.compliant_concept: Calls fclose or close on every path before losing the handle.
false_positive_risks: If implemented as a syntax-only rule: Handles transferred to callers or globals would be reported as leaked.
false_negative_risks: This rule pack contains no detection for this rule; an absence of findings is not evidence of compliance.
Syntax-only detection limit: Leaks on error paths and through ownership transfer need path analysis.

rules.title: Only use values for fsetpos() that are returned from fgetpos()
rules.summary: fsetpos must only be given position values previously obtained from fgetpos on the same file.
rules.noncompliant_concept: Constructing or modifying an fpos_t value manually before calling fsetpos.
rules.compliant_concept: Passes only values returned by a successful fgetpos call.
false_positive_risks: If implemented as a syntax-only rule: Values obtained in other functions from fgetpos look untracked.
false_negative_risks: This rule pack contains no detection for this rule; an absence of findings is not evidence of compliance.
Syntax-only detection limit: Provenance of the fpos_t value needs dataflow across functions.

rules.title: Avoid TOCTOU race conditions while accessing files
rules.summary: Programs must avoid time-of-check/time-of-use races where a file is checked by name and then used by name again.
rules.noncompliant_concept: Calling access or stat on a path and then opening it by the same name.
rules.compliant_concept: Opens the file once and performs checks on the descriptor, or uses exclusive creation flags.

exceptions.summary: Repeated access by file name is allowed when the file lives in a secure directory.
Repeated access by file name is allowed if the program verifies each operation targets the same file.

false_positive_risks: If implemented as a syntax-only rule: Paths in directories controlled only by the program are not exploitable yet match.
false_negative_risks: This rule pack contains no detection for this rule; an absence of findings is not evidence of compliance.
Syntax-only detection limit: Check and use in different functions, or via different path aliases, are missed.

rules.title: Do not access a closed file
rules.summary: A FILE pointer must not be used after its stream has been closed.
rules.noncompliant_concept: Calling fread or fprintf on a stream after fclose.
rules.compliant_concept: Stops using or nulls the pointer after closing.
false_positive_risks: If implemented as a syntax-only rule: Reassigned stream variables after close are compliant but look like reuse.
false_negative_risks: This rule pack contains no detection for this rule; an absence of findings is not evidence of compliance.
Syntax-only detection limit: Closures in other functions or implicit uses of standard streams are missed.

rules.title: Use valid format strings
rules.summary: Format strings must be valid: conversion specifiers, flags, length modifiers, and arguments must match in count and type.
rules.noncompliant_concept: printf with mismatched specifiers, missing arguments, or invalid flag combinations.
rules.compliant_concept: Uses specifiers that exactly match each argument's type and count.
false_positive_risks: If implemented as a syntax-only rule: Without types, compatible argument conversions cannot be confirmed.
false_negative_risks: This rule pack contains no detection for this rule; an absence of findings is not evidence of compliance.
Syntax-only detection limit: Non-literal formats or wrappers lacking format attributes evade checking.

rules.title: Do not use floating-point variables as loop counters
rules.summary: Loop counters must be integer variables, not floating-point, since rounding makes iteration counts unpredictable.
rules.noncompliant_concept: A for loop incrementing a float or double variable to control iterations.
rules.compliant_concept: Uses an integer counter and derives floating values from it.
false_positive_risks: If implemented as a syntax-only rule: Floating variables updated in loops not used as counters may be matched.
false_negative_risks: This rule pack contains no detection for this rule; an absence of findings is not evidence of compliance.
Syntax-only detection limit: Requires types to see the counter is floating; typedefs hide it.

rules.title: Prevent or detect domain and range errors in math functions
rules.summary: Arguments to math functions must be checked to avoid domain and pole errors, and range errors must be detected.
rules.noncompliant_concept: Calling sqrt, log, pow, or similar on unchecked values that may be invalid.
rules.compliant_concept: Validates arguments before the call and checks errno or floating exceptions afterwards.
false_positive_risks: If implemented as a syntax-only rule: Calls on values already constrained by earlier checks would be flagged.
false_negative_risks: This rule pack contains no detection for this rule; an absence of findings is not evidence of compliance.
Syntax-only detection limit: Needs value-range knowledge and knowledge of each function's domain.

rules.title: Ensure that floating-point conversions are within range of the new type
rules.summary: Floating-point conversions to integers or narrower floating types must only occur when the value is representable in the destination type.
rules.noncompliant_concept: Casting a large or NaN double to int or float without range checking.
rules.compliant_concept: Checks the value against destination limits before converting.
false_positive_risks: If implemented as a syntax-only rule: Conversions of values known to be in range are flagged.
false_negative_risks: This rule pack contains no detection for this rule; an absence of findings is not evidence of compliance.
Syntax-only detection limit: Implicit conversions and range knowledge require types and value flow.

rules.title: Preserve precision when converting integral values to floating-point type
rules.summary: Integer values converted to floating types must not lose precision, unless loss is explicitly acceptable.
rules.noncompliant_concept: Converting a large 64-bit integer to float or double where low bits are lost.
rules.compliant_concept: Uses a floating type with enough precision or verifies the value fits exactly.

exceptions.summary: Precision loss in conversion is acceptable when the program requires it; document it with a comment.

false_positive_risks: If implemented as a syntax-only rule: Conversions intentionally tolerating precision loss are flagged.
false_negative_risks: This rule pack contains no detection for this rule; an absence of findings is not evidence of compliance.
Syntax-only detection limit: Implicit conversions need type information to identify.

rules.title: Do not use object representations to compare floating-point values
rules.summary: Floating-point values must not be compared by their object representations (memcmp), since equal values may have different bit patterns.
rules.noncompliant_concept: Using memcmp to compare doubles or structs containing floating members.
rules.compliant_concept: Compares floating values with numeric operators member by member.
false_positive_risks: If implemented as a syntax-only rule: memcmp of non-floating data may be matched without types.
false_negative_risks: This rule pack contains no detection for this rule; an absence of findings is not evidence of compliance.
Syntax-only detection limit: Floating members nested in structs require layout/type knowledge.

rules.title: Avoid undefined behavior while using type-generic macro functions
rules.summary: Type-generic math macros must be invoked with argument types that are valid and compatible for the selected generic function, avoiding mixed decimal/binary or invalid types.
rules.noncompliant_concept: Passing a decimal floating value mixed with a binary floating value to a tgmath macro.
rules.compliant_concept: Converts arguments explicitly to one consistent supported floating type.
false_positive_risks: If implemented as a syntax-only rule: Valid mixed binary floating arguments may appear similar.
false_negative_risks: This rule pack contains no detection for this rule; an absence of findings is not evidence of compliance.
Syntax-only detection limit: Argument types are hidden by variables and typedefs without semantic analysis.

rules.title: Ensure that unsigned integer operations do not wrap
rules.summary: Unsigned arithmetic must not wrap around when the result is used in sensitive contexts such as sizes, indices, or pointer arithmetic.
rules.noncompliant_concept: Computing an allocation size or index via unsigned addition or multiplication without overflow checks.
rules.compliant_concept: Prechecks operands against limits or uses checked arithmetic before the operation.

exceptions.summary: Intentional unsigned wraparound is allowed when the program needs it, with clear comments.
Wraparound checks may be skipped when compile-time reasoning proves wrapping cannot happen.
Unsigned left shifts may wrap, since this behavior is well-defined and commonly expected.

false_positive_risks: If implemented as a syntax-only rule: Most unsigned arithmetic is safe or intentionally modular; flagging every operation is noisy.
false_negative_risks: This rule pack contains no detection for this rule; an absence of findings is not evidence of compliance.
Syntax-only detection limit: Needs value ranges and knowledge of how results flow into sensitive sinks.

rules.title: Ensure that integer conversions do not result in lost or misinterpreted data
rules.summary: Integer conversions, implicit or explicit, must not lose or misinterpret values through truncation or sign changes.
rules.noncompliant_concept: Assigning a size_t to an int or a negative signed value to an unsigned type without checks.
rules.compliant_concept: Validates range before converting or uses types wide enough for all values.

exceptions.summary: Conversions are allowed where the actual implementation's ranges guarantee no data loss.
Integer values representing characters may be converted to character types without range concerns.
Negative compile-time constants may become unsigned of equal or wider width, e.g. (time_t)-1.

false_positive_risks: If implemented as a syntax-only rule: Conversions of values known to fit are reported without range analysis.
false_negative_risks: This rule pack contains no detection for this rule; an absence of findings is not evidence of compliance.
Syntax-only detection limit: Implicit conversions in arithmetic or calls need types; value ranges need flow analysis.

rules.title: Ensure that operations on signed integers do not result in overflow
rules.summary: Signed integer arithmetic must not overflow, because overflow is undefined behavior.
rules.noncompliant_concept: Adding or multiplying signed values from external input without range checks.
rules.compliant_concept: Checks operands against limits before the operation or uses checked arithmetic helpers.
false_positive_risks: If implemented as a syntax-only rule: Operations on small bounded values would be flagged.
false_negative_risks: This rule pack contains no detection for this rule; an absence of findings is not evidence of compliance.
Syntax-only detection limit: Value ranges flow from inputs and across functions; syntax cannot bound them.

rules.title: Ensure that division and remainder operations do not result in divide-by-zero errors
rules.summary: Division and remainder operations must not have a zero divisor.
rules.noncompliant_concept: Dividing by a variable that may be zero, such as untrusted input.
rules.compliant_concept: Checks the divisor for zero before dividing.
false_positive_risks: If implemented as a syntax-only rule: Divisors guaranteed nonzero by earlier logic are flagged.
false_negative_risks: This rule pack contains no detection for this rule; an absence of findings is not evidence of compliance.
Syntax-only detection limit: Divisor values computed elsewhere need dataflow.

rules.title: Do not shift an expression by a negative number of bits or by greater than or equal to the number of bits that exist in the operand
rules.summary: Shift amounts must be non-negative and less than the width of the promoted left operand.
rules.noncompliant_concept: Shifting by a variable amount that may exceed the type's width or be negative.
rules.compliant_concept: Validates the shift amount against the operand precision before shifting.
false_positive_risks: If implemented as a syntax-only rule: Variable shift amounts already range-checked are flagged.
false_negative_risks: This rule pack contains no detection for this rule; an absence of findings is not evidence of compliance.
Syntax-only detection limit: Needs operand width after promotion and shift value ranges.

rules.title: Use correct integer precisions
rules.summary: The precision of integer types must be computed correctly, not inferred from sizeof times CHAR_BIT, which may include padding bits.
rules.noncompliant_concept: Using sizeof(type) * CHAR_BIT as a shift limit or bit count.
rules.compliant_concept: Computes precision via popcount of the max value or uses width macros.
false_positive_risks: If implemented as a syntax-only rule: On most platforms size and precision match; sizeof*CHAR_BIT uses in harmless contexts are flagged.
false_negative_risks: This rule pack contains no detection for this rule; an absence of findings is not evidence of compliance.
Syntax-only detection limit: Precision assumptions made with hardcoded constants are missed.

rules.title: Converting a pointer to integer or integer to pointer
rules.summary: Conversions between pointers and integers are implementation-defined and should be avoided except with intptr_t/uintptr_t via valid pointers.
rules.noncompliant_concept: Casting a pointer to int or long, or an arbitrary integer to a pointer.
rules.compliant_concept: Uses intptr_t or uintptr_t for round-trip conversions of valid pointers.

exceptions.summary: Converting the integer constant 0 to a pointer, producing a null pointer, is allowed.
Valid void pointers may round-trip through intptr_t or uintptr_t without loss.
An in-range integer may be cast to void* and back, provided the pointer is never dereferenced.

false_positive_risks: If implemented as a syntax-only rule: Conversions to uintptr_t or null-pointer constants would match without types.
false_negative_risks: This rule pack contains no detection for this rule; an absence of findings is not evidence of compliance.
Syntax-only detection limit: Conversions hidden behind typedefs or macros need type resolution.

rules.title: Do not access freed memory
rules.summary: Memory must not be accessed or its pointer value used after it has been freed.
rules.noncompliant_concept: Dereferencing or reusing a pointer after free or a successful realloc.
rules.compliant_concept: Stops using the pointer after free, setting it to null or reassigning it.
false_positive_risks: If implemented as a syntax-only rule: Reassigned pointers or conditional frees cause spurious use-after-free matches.
false_negative_risks: This rule pack contains no detection for this rule; an absence of findings is not evidence of compliance.
