rules.title: Free dynamically allocated memory when no longer needed
rules.summary: Dynamically allocated memory must be freed before the last pointer to it is lost.
rules.noncompliant_concept: Returning or exiting scope while the only pointer to an allocation is discarded.
rules.compliant_concept: Frees allocations on every path or transfers ownership explicitly.

exceptions.summary: Memory need not be freed if held by a pointer that lives until program termination.

false_positive_risks: If implemented as a syntax-only rule: Ownership transfers to callers or global structures look like leaks.
false_negative_risks: This rule pack contains no detection for this rule; an absence of findings is not evidence of compliance.
Syntax-only detection limit: Leaks along error paths and via aliasing need path-sensitive analysis.

rules.title: Allocate and copy structures containing a flexible array member dynamically
rules.summary: Structures with flexible array members must be allocated dynamically with room for the array, and copied with memcpy accounting for its size, not by assignment.
rules.noncompliant_concept: Declaring such a struct as a local, or copying it via struct assignment or pass-by-value.
rules.compliant_concept: Allocates with malloc including array size and copies with memcpy using full size.
false_positive_risks: If implemented as a syntax-only rule: Needs knowing the struct type has a flexible array member.
false_negative_risks: This rule pack contains no detection for this rule; an absence of findings is not evidence of compliance.
Syntax-only detection limit: Copies through typedefs or passed-by-value parameters require type resolution.

rules.title: Only free memory allocated dynamically
rules.summary: free and realloc must only receive pointers obtained from memory allocation functions that have not already been freed.
rules.noncompliant_concept: Freeing a stack array, string literal, or pointer offset into an allocation.
rules.compliant_concept: Frees only the exact pointer returned by an allocation function.
false_positive_risks: If implemented as a syntax-only rule: Pointers whose provenance is unclear (parameters) look suspicious.
false_negative_risks: This rule pack contains no detection for this rule; an absence of findings is not evidence of compliance.
Syntax-only detection limit: Provenance through parameters, globals, or pointer arithmetic needs dataflow.

rules.title: Allocate sufficient memory for an object
rules.summary: Allocation size computations must yield enough bytes for the intended object, using the correct type size and avoiding overflow or truncation.
rules.noncompliant_concept: malloc(sizeof(ptr)) instead of sizeof(*ptr), or n*size computed without overflow checks.
rules.compliant_concept: Uses sizeof of the pointee type and checks multiplications before allocating.
false_positive_risks: If implemented as a syntax-only rule: Allocations deliberately sized differently (headers, flexible arrays) appear mismatched.
false_negative_risks: This rule pack contains no detection for this rule; an absence of findings is not evidence of compliance.
Syntax-only detection limit: Sizes computed earlier or via helpers hide insufficient amounts.

rules.title: Do not modify the alignment of objects by calling realloc()
rules.summary: realloc must not be used on objects requiring stricter alignment than malloc guarantees, since the result may lose that alignment.
rules.noncompliant_concept: Calling realloc on a pointer returned by aligned_alloc with large alignment.
rules.compliant_concept: Allocates a new aligned block and copies data manually instead of realloc.
false_positive_risks: If implemented as a syntax-only rule: realloc on ordinarily allocated memory would be flagged without provenance.
false_negative_risks: This rule pack contains no detection for this rule; an absence of findings is not evidence of compliance.
Syntax-only detection limit: Needs to track that the pointer came from an over-aligned allocation.

rules.title: Do not use the rand() function for generating pseudorandom numbers
rules.summary: rand() must not be used where quality or unpredictability of pseudorandom numbers matters, such as security contexts.
rules.noncompliant_concept: Calling rand() to generate tokens, keys, or other security-relevant values.
rules.compliant_concept: Uses a cryptographically suitable generator such as platform CSPRNG APIs.
false_positive_risks: Uses of rand() for non-security purposes are reported; the rule itself makes no such distinction.
false_negative_risks: Engines do not preprocess: code produced by macro expansion, conditional compilation, or code generation is not analyzed.
Calls through function pointers to rand are not detected.

implementation.coverage_note: Every rand() call in C is reported; C++ translation units are covered by the MSC50-CPP rule, whose findings also evidence MSC30-C.

rules.title: Properly seed pseudorandom number generators
rules.summary: Pseudorandom generators must be seeded with an unpredictable value so their output sequence differs across runs.
rules.noncompliant_concept: Calling random() without seeding, or seeding with a constant or time value.
rules.compliant_concept: Seeds the generator from a high-entropy source.
false_positive_risks: If implemented as a syntax-only rule: Deterministic seeding intended for reproducible tests is flagged.
false_negative_risks: This rule pack contains no detection for this rule; an absence of findings is not evidence of compliance.
Syntax-only detection limit: Seeds that look variable but derive from predictable sources are missed.

rules.title: Do not pass invalid data to the asctime() function
rules.summary: asctime() must only receive struct tm values whose fields are in ranges that cannot overflow its fixed internal buffer.
rules.noncompliant_concept: Passing an unvalidated struct tm to asctime.
rules.compliant_concept: Uses strftime with a bounded buffer instead of asctime.
false_positive_risks: If implemented as a syntax-only rule: asctime calls on validated or library-produced tm values are flagged.
false_negative_risks: This rule pack contains no detection for this rule; an absence of findings is not evidence of compliance.
Syntax-only detection limit: asctime_r or wrappers with the same flaw may be missed.

rules.title: Ensure that control never reaches the end of a non-void function
rules.summary: Control must not reach the end of a non-void function without a return statement.
rules.noncompliant_concept: A non-void function with a path that falls off the closing brace.
rules.compliant_concept: Ensures every path returns a value or calls a noreturn function.

exceptions.summary: main() may end without a return statement, since reaching its end implicitly returns 0.
A path may lack a return value if it is never taken and invokes a _Noreturn function.

false_positive_risks: If implemented as a syntax-only rule: Paths ending in noreturn calls or exhaustive switches look like fall-off.
false_negative_risks: This rule pack contains no detection for this rule; an absence of findings is not evidence of compliance.
Syntax-only detection limit: Requires control-flow graph reasoning beyond purely textual matching.

rules.title: Do not treat a predefined identifier as an object if it might only be implemented as a macro
rules.summary: Standard library identifiers that may be implemented only as macros, like assert or errno, must not be treated as objects or functions.
rules.noncompliant_concept: Taking the address of assert or redeclaring errno as an extern int.
rules.compliant_concept: Uses the macros as intended and includes the proper headers.
false_positive_risks: If implemented as a syntax-only rule: Few; parenthesized function names with real function implementations may match.
false_negative_risks: This rule pack contains no detection for this rule; an absence of findings is not evidence of compliance.
Syntax-only detection limit: Indirect uses via other macros or token pasting are missed.

rules.title: Do not call va_arg() on a va_list that has an indeterminate value
rules.summary: A va_list whose value is indeterminate, e.g., after being passed to a function that used va_arg, must not be used again without va_end/va_start or va_copy.
rules.noncompliant_concept: Calling va_arg on a va_list after passing it to vprintf or a helper.
rules.compliant_concept: Calls va_end and va_start again, or passes a va_copy to the helper.
false_positive_risks: If implemented as a syntax-only rule: Helpers taking va_list by pointer keep it determinate yet match.
false_negative_risks: This rule pack contains no detection for this rule; an absence of findings is not evidence of compliance.
Syntax-only detection limit: Needs to know whether the callee consumed the va_list.

rules.title: Do not violate constraints
rules.summary: Code must not violate constraints of the C Standard, which require diagnostics, such as inline functions with external linkage referencing internal-linkage objects.
rules.noncompliant_concept: An extern inline function referencing a static object or defining a modifiable static.
rules.compliant_concept: Adjusts linkage, qualifiers, or structure so all language constraints are satisfied.
false_positive_risks: If implemented as a syntax-only rule: Compiler extensions accepted intentionally may be reported.
false_negative_risks: This rule pack contains no detection for this rule; an absence of findings is not evidence of compliance.
Syntax-only detection limit: Constraints are numerous; a syntax detector can cover only a few patterns.

rules.title: Never hard code sensitive information
rules.summary: Sensitive data such as passwords or cryptographic keys must not be embedded in source code or binaries.
rules.noncompliant_concept: Assigning a literal password or key string to a variable used for authentication.
rules.compliant_concept: Obtains secrets at runtime from protected storage and clears them after use.
false_positive_risks: If implemented as a syntax-only rule: Literals named like secrets that are placeholders or test data are flagged.
false_negative_risks: This rule pack contains no detection for this rule; an absence of findings is not evidence of compliance.
Syntax-only detection limit: Secrets with innocuous names or obfuscated constants are missed.

rules.title: Use the readlink() function properly
rules.summary: readlink() does not null-terminate its output, so callers must reserve space and terminate the buffer using the returned length after checking for errors.
rules.noncompliant_concept: Passing sizeof(buf) to readlink and using the buffer as a string.
rules.compliant_concept: Passes size minus one, checks for -1, and writes the terminator at the returned length.
false_positive_risks: If implemented as a syntax-only rule: Correct termination performed in a helper may be missed, causing false alarms.
false_negative_risks: This rule pack contains no detection for this rule; an absence of findings is not evidence of compliance.
Syntax-only detection limit: Termination at the wrong index or unchecked -1 return requires value reasoning.

rules.title: Do not call putenv() with a pointer to an automatic variable as the argument
rules.summary: putenv must not be given a pointer to automatic storage, since the environment keeps the pointer after the function returns.
rules.noncompliant_concept: Calling putenv with a local character array.
rules.compliant_concept: Uses static or heap storage, or setenv which copies the string.
false_positive_risks: None expected for direct automatic arrays.
false_negative_risks: Automatic storage reached through pointer aliases or helper functions is not tracked.
Engines do not preprocess: code produced by macro expansion, conditional compilation, or code generation is not analyzed.

implementation.coverage_note: Same-function putenv() of a non-static local character array.

rules.title: Avoid race conditions while checking for the existence of a symbolic link
rules.summary: Checks for symbolic links must not be separated from the subsequent file use by name, avoiding TOCTOU races.
rules.noncompliant_concept: Calling lstat on a path and then opening the same path.
rules.compliant_concept: Opens with O_NOFOLLOW then verifies via fstat on the descriptor.
false_positive_risks: If implemented as a syntax-only rule: Paths in protected directories make the sequence safe yet match.
false_negative_risks: This rule pack contains no detection for this rule; an absence of findings is not evidence of compliance.
Syntax-only detection limit: Check and use split across functions or path variants are missed.

rules.title: Observe correct revocation order while relinquishing privileges
rules.summary: When dropping privileges, supplementary and group privileges must be relinquished before user privileges.
rules.noncompliant_concept: Calling setuid before setgid when dropping root privileges.
rules.compliant_concept: Drops supplementary groups, then group id, then user id.
false_positive_risks: Programs that intentionally change the effective user ID temporarily and later restore it may be reported.
false_negative_risks: Revocation order split across functions is not detected.
Engines do not preprocess: code produced by macro expansion, conditional compilation, or code generation is not analyzed.

implementation.coverage_note: Same-function user-ID change followed by a group-ID or supplementary-group change.

rules.title: Ensure that privilege relinquishment is successful
rules.summary: Privilege relinquishment calls must be checked for success, and the program must verify privileges cannot be regained.
rules.noncompliant_concept: Calling setuid without checking its return value.
rules.compliant_concept: Checks every setuid/setgid result and confirms privileges cannot be restored.
false_positive_risks: Calls whose failure is handled by a later explicit privilege check are reported.
false_negative_risks: Verification that privileges cannot be regained after a successful call is not checked.
Return values stored but never tested are not detected.
Engines do not preprocess: code produced by macro expansion, conditional compilation, or code generation is not analyzed.

implementation.coverage_note: set*id calls whose return value is discarded.

rules.title: Beware of race conditions when using fork and file descriptors
rules.summary: File descriptors inherited across fork must not be used concurrently by parent and child in ways that cause races on the same file.
rules.noncompliant_concept: Opening a file before fork and having both processes read or write it.
rules.compliant_concept: Opens files after forking or coordinates access between processes.
false_positive_risks: If implemented as a syntax-only rule: Descriptors deliberately shared (e.g., pipes) appear risky.
false_negative_risks: This rule pack contains no detection for this rule; an absence of findings is not evidence of compliance.
Syntax-only detection limit: Use of inherited descriptors in separate functions or processes is hard to correlate.

rules.title: Use the correct byte ordering when transferring data between systems
rules.summary: Multi-byte values exchanged across systems must be converted between host and network byte order.
rules.noncompliant_concept: Sending or receiving integers over a socket without htonl/ntohl.
rules.compliant_concept: Applies byte-order conversion functions on send and receive.
false_positive_risks: If implemented as a syntax-only rule: Values that are single bytes or already converted elsewhere are flagged.
false_negative_risks: This rule pack contains no detection for this rule; an absence of findings is not evidence of compliance.
Syntax-only detection limit: Protocol semantics determine whether conversion is needed; syntax cannot tell.

rules.title: Do not use signals to terminate threads
rules.summary: Signals must not be used to terminate individual threads, since uncaught signals terminate the entire process.
rules.noncompliant_concept: Calling pthread_kill with SIGTERM or SIGKILL to stop a thread.
rules.compliant_concept: Uses pthread_cancel or cooperative shutdown flags.
false_positive_risks: Programs that intend to terminate the whole process from a thread are reported, which the rule also discourages.
false_negative_risks: Signals passed through variables, raise() and kill() targeting the own process are not detected.
Engines do not preprocess: code produced by macro expansion, conditional compilation, or code generation is not analyzed.

implementation.coverage_note: pthread_kill() with a literal process-terminating signal.

rules.title: Do not use threads that can be canceled asynchronously
rules.summary: Threads must not be configured for asynchronous cancellation, since few functions are async-cancel-safe.
rules.noncompliant_concept: Calling pthread_setcanceltype with PTHREAD_CANCEL_ASYNCHRONOUS.
rules.compliant_concept: Uses deferred cancellation with explicit cancellation points.
false_positive_risks: None expected.
false_negative_risks: A cancellation type passed through a variable is not resolved.
Engines do not preprocess: code produced by macro expansion, conditional compilation, or code generation is not analyzed.

rules.title: Do not unlock or destroy another POSIX thread's mutex
rules.summary: A POSIX mutex must be unlocked only by the thread owning it, and must not be destroyed while still in use.
rules.noncompliant_concept: Destroying a mutex while other threads may still lock it, or unlocking from a non-owner thread.
rules.compliant_concept: Joins threads before destroying, and ensures the locking thread unlocks.
false_positive_risks: If implemented as a syntax-only rule: Destroy calls after all threads have joined look suspicious.
false_negative_risks: This rule pack contains no detection for this rule; an absence of findings is not evidence of compliance.
Syntax-only detection limit: Ownership and thread lifetimes require concurrency modeling.

rules.title: When data must be accessed by multiple threads, provide a mutex and guarantee no adjacent data is also accessed
rules.summary: Data shared among threads requires a mutex, and adjacent data (like neighboring bit-fields) sharing storage must also be protected.
rules.noncompliant_concept: Threads modifying adjacent bit-fields or packed fields with separate or no locks.
rules.compliant_concept: Uses one mutex for all data in a shared storage unit, or separates the data.
false_positive_risks: If implemented as a syntax-only rule: Accesses in single-threaded contexts appear unprotected.
false_negative_risks: This rule pack contains no detection for this rule; an absence of findings is not evidence of compliance.
Syntax-only detection limit: Determining shared objects and memory adjacency requires semantic analysis.

rules.title: Declare objects shared between POSIX threads with appropriate storage durations
rules.summary: Objects shared between POSIX threads must have storage duration covering all threads that access them.
rules.noncompliant_concept: Passing a local variable address to pthread_create and returning before the thread finishes.
rules.compliant_concept: Uses static or heap storage, or joins the thread before the local's scope ends.
false_positive_risks: If implemented as a syntax-only rule: Local addresses passed when the creator joins promptly are safe.
false_negative_risks: This rule pack contains no detection for this rule; an absence of findings is not evidence of compliance.
Syntax-only detection limit: Escapes through structures and helper functions are invisible.

rules.title: Avoid deadlock with POSIX threads by locking in predefined order
rules.summary: POSIX mutexes must be acquired in a predefined consistent order by all threads to prevent deadlock.
rules.noncompliant_concept: Locking mutexes A then B in one thread and B then A in another.
rules.compliant_concept: Imposes a global lock ordering such as by address.
false_positive_risks: If implemented as a syntax-only rule: Multiple locks taken in consistent order look identical to inverted ones locally.
false_negative_risks: This rule pack contains no detection for this rule; an absence of findings is not evidence of compliance.
Syntax-only detection limit: Inversions span functions and threads.

rules.title: Do not perform operations that can block while holding a POSIX lock
rules.summary: Operations that may block, such as I/O, must not be performed while holding a POSIX lock.
rules.noncompliant_concept: Calling recv or read inside a region guarded by pthread_mutex_lock.
rules.compliant_concept: Releases the lock before blocking or uses nonblocking operations.

exceptions.summary: A thread may wait for another lock while holding locks, if a deadlock-free ordering is used.

false_positive_risks: If implemented as a syntax-only rule: Nonblocking descriptors or brief operations would be flagged.
false_negative_risks: This rule pack contains no detection for this rule; an absence of findings is not evidence of compliance.
Syntax-only detection limit: Blocking calls inside callees during critical sections are missed.

rules.title: Do not use more than one mutex for concurrent waiting operations on a condition variable
rules.summary: All threads waiting concurrently on the same condition variable must use the same mutex.
rules.noncompliant_concept: Waiting on one condition variable with different mutexes in different threads.
rules.compliant_concept: Associates each condition variable with exactly one mutex.
false_positive_risks: If implemented as a syntax-only rule: Different mutex expressions may alias the same object.
false_negative_risks: This rule pack contains no detection for this rule; an absence of findings is not evidence of compliance.
Syntax-only detection limit: Requires matching runtime condition variables and mutexes across threads.

rules.title: Detect and handle POSIX library errors
rules.summary: Return values of POSIX library functions indicating errors must be checked and handled.
rules.noncompliant_concept: Ignoring the return of pthread_mutex_lock, fmemopen, or similar POSIX calls.
rules.compliant_concept: Checks each return value or errno per the function's documented convention.

exceptions.summary: This exception has been withdrawn; it no longer permits anything.
The ERR33-C-EX1 allowance for ignoring certain return values also applies here.

false_positive_risks: If implemented as a syntax-only rule: Calls whose failure is harmless or checked later are flagged.
false_negative_risks: This rule pack contains no detection for this rule; an absence of findings is not evidence of compliance.
Syntax-only detection limit: Checking against the wrong error value looks compliant syntactically.

rules.title: Do not create a universal character name through concatenation
rules.summary: Universal character names must not be formed by token concatenation in macros, which is undefined behavior.
rules.noncompliant_concept: Using ## to paste \u with hex digits into a universal character name.
rules.compliant_concept: Writes the full universal character name literally.
false_positive_risks: If implemented as a syntax-only rule: Pasting that merely includes backslashes without forming a UCN may match.
false_negative_risks: This rule pack contains no detection for this rule; an absence of findings is not evidence of compliance.
Syntax-only detection limit: Indirect macro expansions forming UCNs are hard to detect without preprocessing.

rules.title: Avoid side effects in arguments to unsafe macros
rules.summary: Arguments with side effects must not be passed to unsafe macros that evaluate parameters zero or multiple times, including assert.
rules.noncompliant_concept: Invoking a macro like ABS(x++) or assert(i++ > 0).
rules.compliant_concept: Moves side effects out of the macro argument or uses an inline function.

exceptions.summary: An unsafe macro may receive a function-call argument if that function has no side effects.

false_positive_risks: If implemented as a syntax-only rule: Safe macros evaluating parameters once look like unsafe ones without expansion.
false_negative_risks: This rule pack contains no detection for this rule; an absence of findings is not evidence of compliance.
Syntax-only detection limit: Function-call arguments with hidden side effects are hard to judge.

rules.title: Do not use preprocessor directives in invocations of function-like macros
rules.summary: Preprocessor directives must not appear inside the argument list of a function-like macro invocation.
rules.noncompliant_concept: Placing #ifdef blocks within the arguments of a call that may be a macro like memcpy.
rules.compliant_concept: Moves conditional compilation outside the macro call.
false_positive_risks: If implemented as a syntax-only rule: Calls to true functions (not macros) with embedded directives are flagged.
false_negative_risks: This rule pack contains no detection for this rule; an absence of findings is not evidence of compliance.
Syntax-only detection limit: Whether the called name is a macro depends on headers and configuration.

rules.title: Call only asynchronous-safe functions within signal handlers
rules.summary: Signal handlers may only call asynchronous-safe functions.
rules.noncompliant_concept: Calling printf, malloc, or free inside a signal handler.
rules.compliant_concept: Sets a volatile sig_atomic_t flag in the handler and does work elsewhere.
false_positive_risks: If implemented as a syntax-only rule: Handlers invoked only synchronously may legitimately call more functions.
false_negative_risks: This rule pack contains no detection for this rule; an absence of findings is not evidence of compliance.
Syntax-only detection limit: Unsafe calls in helpers called by handlers, or handlers registered via variables, are missed.

rules.title: Do not access shared objects in signal handlers
rules.summary: Signal handlers must not access shared objects other than lock-free atomics or volatile sig_atomic_t variables.
rules.noncompliant_concept: Modifying a global struct or non-atomic variable inside a handler.
rules.compliant_concept: Restricts handler access to volatile sig_atomic_t or lock-free atomic objects.

exceptions.summary: After signal() fails returning SIG_ERR, the handler may rely on errno's indeterminate value.

false_positive_risks: If implemented as a syntax-only rule: Accesses to handler-local data or handler-only state may be flagged.
false_negative_risks: This rule pack contains no detection for this rule; an absence of findings is not evidence of compliance.
Syntax-only detection limit: Shared accesses inside helper functions or via pointers are missed.

rules.title: Do not call signal() from within interruptible signal handlers
rules.summary: A signal handler must not call signal() to reinstall itself where signals may interrupt it, creating race conditions.
rules.noncompliant_concept: Calling signal(sig, handler) from within the handler on nonpersistent platforms.
rules.compliant_concept: Uses sigaction with persistent handlers instead of reinstalling.

exceptions.summary: With persistent handlers, a handler may change its own signal's disposition, e.g. reset to default.

false_positive_risks: If implemented as a syntax-only rule: Platforms with persistent handlers or masked signals make it safe.
false_negative_risks: This rule pack contains no detection for this rule; an absence of findings is not evidence of compliance.
Syntax-only detection limit: Reinstallation done via helper functions is missed.

rules.title: Do not return from a computational exception signal handler
rules.summary: Signal handlers for computational exceptions like SIGFPE, SIGILL, or SIGSEGV must not return.
rules.noncompliant_concept: A SIGFPE handler that returns normally after setting a flag.
rules.compliant_concept: Terminates via abort or _Exit from such handlers, or avoids handling them.
false_positive_risks: If implemented as a syntax-only rule: Handlers registered for multiple signals may return only for non-computational ones.
false_negative_risks: This rule pack contains no detection for this rule; an absence of findings is not evidence of compliance.
Syntax-only detection limit: Mapping handlers to the signals they handle often spans functions.

rules.title: Do not attempt to modify string literals
rules.summary: String literals must not be modified, as their storage may be read-only.
rules.noncompliant_concept: Writing through a char pointer initialized with a string literal, or via strrchr results.
rules.compliant_concept: Copies literals into modifiable arrays before changes, using const char pointers otherwise.
false_positive_risks: If implemented as a syntax-only rule: Pointers reassigned to writable buffers before modification are flagged.
false_negative_risks: This rule pack contains no detection for this rule; an absence of findings is not evidence of compliance.
Syntax-only detection limit: Literal pointers flowing through functions like strchr or parameters are missed.

rules.title: Guarantee that storage for strings has sufficient space for character data and the null terminator
rules.summary: Destination buffers for string data must have space for all characters plus the null terminator.
rules.noncompliant_concept: Using strcpy, gets, or sprintf into fixed buffers without size checks, or off-by-one sizing.
rules.compliant_concept: Validates lengths before copying or uses bounded functions with correct sizes.
false_positive_risks: None expected for gets(); a %s conversion reading into a buffer proven large enough by context is still reported.
false_negative_risks: strcpy, strcat, sprintf, manual loops, and off-by-one sizing require bounds analysis and are not detected.
Field widths larger than the destination are not compared with its size.
Engines do not preprocess: code produced by macro expansion, conditional compilation, or code generation is not analyzed.

implementation.coverage_note: Covers the unbounded-input subset: gets() and width-less %s/%[ scanf conversions.

rules.title: Do not pass a non-null-terminated character sequence to a library function that expects a string
rules.summary: Character sequences passed to functions expecting strings must be null-terminated.
rules.noncompliant_concept: Passing a strncpy result or exactly filled buffer to strlen or printf.
rules.compliant_concept: Ensures explicit termination after bounded copies.
false_positive_risks: If implemented as a syntax-only rule: strncpy followed by explicit termination elsewhere is flagged.
false_negative_risks: This rule pack contains no detection for this rule; an absence of findings is not evidence of compliance.
Syntax-only detection limit: Termination depends on runtime lengths and buffers from other functions.

rules.title: Cast characters to unsigned char before converting to larger integer sizes
rules.summary: Plain or signed char values must be converted to unsigned char before widening to larger integer types.
rules.noncompliant_concept: Assigning a char directly to an int used as an index or comparison value.
rules.compliant_concept: Casts to unsigned char before widening.

exceptions.summary: Chars used as small arithmetic integers, not character data, need not be cast to unsigned char.

false_positive_risks: If implemented as a syntax-only rule: Values known to be in ASCII range are flagged.
false_negative_risks: This rule pack contains no detection for this rule; an absence of findings is not evidence of compliance.
Syntax-only detection limit: Implicit widening in expressions needs type resolution.

rules.title: Arguments to character-handling functions must be representable as an unsigned char
rules.summary: Arguments to ctype functions must be representable as unsigned char or equal EOF.
rules.noncompliant_concept: Calling isspace or toupper with a plain char that may be negative.
rules.compliant_concept: Casts the argument to unsigned char before calling.
false_positive_risks: If implemented as a syntax-only rule: Arguments known to be valid ints (e.g., from getc) are flagged.
false_negative_risks: This rule pack contains no detection for this rule; an absence of findings is not evidence of compliance.
Syntax-only detection limit: Signedness of argument types requires semantic analysis.

rules.title: Do not confuse narrow and wide character strings and functions
rules.summary: Narrow string functions must not be given wide strings and vice versa.
rules.noncompliant_concept: Passing a wchar_t buffer to strlen or a char buffer to wcscpy.
rules.compliant_concept: Pairs narrow strings with narrow functions and wide with wide.
false_positive_risks: If implemented as a syntax-only rule: Casted buffers deliberately reinterpreted may be flagged.
false_negative_risks: This rule pack contains no detection for this rule; an absence of findings is not evidence of compliance.
Syntax-only detection limit: Requires argument types; casts silence type mismatches.

rules.title: Properly pair allocation and deallocation functions
rules.summary: Windows memory allocation functions must be paired with their matching deallocation functions.
rules.noncompliant_concept: Freeing LocalAlloc memory with free, or malloc memory with GlobalFree.
rules.compliant_concept: Uses the deallocator corresponding to each allocator.
false_positive_risks: If implemented as a syntax-only rule: Allocations converted by helper wrappers look mismatched.
false_negative_risks: This rule pack contains no detection for this rule; an absence of findings is not evidence of compliance.
Syntax-only detection limit: Allocator and deallocator separated across functions are not linked.
